Select the ESPHome module to use as a Bluetooth proxy.
The Bluetooth MAC is detected automatically and shown for identification.

mqtt_broker.description: The ESP32 must publish its MAC on `{mac_topic}` at startup (auto-discovery in next step, timeout {timeout}s).

mqtt_mac.description:
MQTT topic: `{topic}`
Auto-discovered MAC: **{mac_found}** (empty = not found → enter manually).

abort.no_esphome_device: No ESPHome module found. Check that the ESPHome integration is configured in Home Assistant.

error.invalid_mac: Invalid MAC address — expected format: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF

error.invalid_uuid: Invalid UUID — 6 hex characters required (e.g. 9c0300), 8 for a scene. Check that the bytes are not reversed.

menu_options.advanced_settings: Change the Jeedom key / controller MAC

advanced_settings.title: Jeedom key / Controller MAC
advanced_settings.description:
**Current Jeedom key:** `{current_key}`
**Current controller MAC:** `{current_mac}`

Changing the Jeedom key requires re-pairing all modules. Leave a field empty to keep the current value.

**Transmission method** (local Bluetooth controller only): "Linux kernel" transmits without the hcitool tool and without interrupting scanning; if it fails, the integration falls back to hcitool.

data.jeedom_key: Jeedom key (leave empty to keep current)
data.mac: BLE controller MAC (HCI controller or ESP32 — leave empty to keep current)

import_export.title: Export / Import modules
import_export.description:
**{count}** module(s) configured. Copy the Export field to back up the list; paste a list into the Import field to add modules.

UUIDs already present are ignored on import.

add.title: Add a module
add.description:
Recently detected BLE modules: **{pending}** ("—": none; press the module's pairing button first)

**UUID format:**
— **logs/Jeedom** format: UUID as shown in the logs (e.g. `9c0300`)
— **module label** format: reversed bytes (e.g. `00039c` → converted to `9c0300`)

If a detected module is selected, the UUID field is ignored. A scene has an 8-character identifier; the easiest way is to find it with "Search a module's scenes".

data.uuid: UUID (6 hex characters, 8 for a scene)
data.name: Name (leave empty for automatic name)
data.mac: BLE MAC address of the module (optional)

edit.title: Edit module
edit.description:
Current UUID: `{current_uuid}` — Label equivalent: `{reversed_uuid}`

Choose the format in which you are entering the new UUID.

confirm_remove.title: Remove {name}
confirm_remove.description:
How do you want to remove module **{name}** (`{uuid}`)?

_Note: the "Unpair" option waits for you to press the physical button on the module. The module is removed from Home Assistant only if it confirms unpairing; otherwise it is kept._

scenes.title: Search a module's scenes
scenes.description: Home Assistant asks the module for the scenes it has stored, then creates a scene entity for each one. The search takes a few seconds.

scenes_result.title: Scenes found
scenes_result.description:
Scenes announced by the module: **{found}** ("—": no reply or no scene)

New scenes created: **{created}**

rebind.title: Re-pair a module
rebind.description:
Use this for a module that no longer obeys Home Assistant (reset, or paired with another controller).

After confirming, press the module's physical button **once**: Home Assistant will send it the pairing frame.

error.already_exists: A module with this UUID already exists
error.invalid_json: Invalid list — paste the export lines, or a complete JSON object in braces
error.invalid_key: Invalid Jeedom key — 24 hex characters required
error.invalid_mac: Invalid MAC address — expected format: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
error.invalid_service: Invalid service name — enter the service declared in the ESPHome firmware (e.g. odace_send)
error.invalid_uuid: Invalid UUID — 6 hex characters required (e.g. 9c0300), 8 for a scene. Check that the bytes are not reversed.
error.send_failed: The request could not be sent to the module (see the logs)

abort.no_esphome_device: No ESPHome device found. Check that the ESPHome integration is configured in Home Assistant.
abort.no_scene_source: No module able to list its scenes (dcl, shutter or generic) is configured.
abort.unpair_unpaired: Module **{name}** (`{uuid}`) confirmed unpairing. It has been removed from Home Assistant.
abort.unpair_paired:
Module **{name}** (`{uuid}`) was not paired: the frame has just **paired** it instead of unpairing it. It is kept in Home Assistant.

To unpair it, run "Unpair the module, then remove from HA" again and press its button once more.
abort.unpair_no_press: No press detected on the button of module **{name}** (`{uuid}`) within 60 seconds. Unpairing is cancelled and the module is kept.
abort.unpair_no_answer:
The unpairing frame was sent, but module **{name}** (`{uuid}`) did not reply. It is kept in Home Assistant.

Move the controller closer or try again. If the button cannot be reached, reset the module (10 s press) then choose "Remove from HA only".
abort.unpair_send_failed: The unpairing frame could not be sent (see the logs). Module **{name}** (`{uuid}`) is kept.
abort.rebind_armed:
Press the physical button of module **{name}** (`{uuid}`) **once** within 30 minutes: Home Assistant will send it the pairing frame.

If the module was still paired, it unpairs instead of pairing. An alert then appears in **Settings → Repairs**: press its button a second time.
abort.no_pairable_module: No controllable module (dcl, shutter, plug or generic) is configured.

progress.unpair_wait:
Press the physical button of module **{name}** (`{uuid}`) **once**, now.

Home Assistant waits 60 seconds for the press, sends the unpairing frame, then waits for the module's reply. This window updates by itself.

options.unpair_and_remove: Unpair the module, then remove from HA

options.hcitool: hcitool — direct commands to the adapter (historical)
options.mgmt: Linux kernel — without hcitool, does not interrupt scanning (experimental)

module_unpaired.title: Odace module {name} unpaired
module_unpaired.description:
Module **{name}** (`{uuid}`) was already paired: the pairing frame sent by Home Assistant has **unpaired** it. It no longer obeys commands.

Press its physical button once more within 30 minutes: Home Assistant will pair it again and this alert will disappear. After that delay, use **Configure → Re-pair a module**.

send_command.name: Send a command
send_command.description: Sends an Odace SFSP BLE frame

test_send.name: Transmission test (diagnostic)
test_send.description: Sends a command to a module and returns the trace of what the adapter actually transmitted. Local Bluetooth controller mode only.

uuid.name: Module UUID
uuid.description: Module to control, for example a DCL.

method.name: Method
method.description: hcitool or mgmt (kernel). Defaults to the method set in the advanced settings.
